cards.heading: supply and borrow
cards.body: DeFi lending works like a peer-to-pool system. Suppliers deposit assets into a smart contract pool and earn interest. Borrowers take assets from the pool by posting collateral and paying interest.

cards.heading: how interest rates work
cards.body: Rates are set by supply and demand. When many people borrow, the utilization rate rises and interest goes up — incentivizing more suppliers. Protocols like Aave and Compound automate this with rate curves.

cards.text: Unlike a bank, there's no credit check. Anyone with collateral can borrow instantly. The smart contract is the only intermediary.

cards.heading: why >100% collateral?
cards.body: In DeFi, there's no identity or credit score. The only guarantee is your collateral. To protect lenders, protocols require you to deposit more value than you borrow — typically 120-150% of the loan value.

cards.text: Overcollateralization means if you want to borrow $1,000, you might need to lock up $1,500 in ETH. The extra cushion protects against price drops.

cards.heading: the number that keeps you safe
cards.body: Health Factor = (Collateral Value × Liquidation Threshold) / Borrow Value. Above 1.0, you're safe. At 1.0, you get liquidated. Most users aim to stay above 1.5 for a comfortable buffer.

cards.heading: what happens at liquidation
cards.body: When HF drops to 1.0, a liquidator repays part of your debt and takes your collateral at a discount (typically 5-10% bonus). You lose your collateral and still owe the remaining debt minus what was repaid.

cards.text: A health factor of 1.1 means a 10% drop in your collateral's price could trigger liquidation. Always monitor your positions.

cards.heading: two different numbers
cards.body: LTV (Loan-to-Value) is the maximum you can borrow against your collateral — e.g., 75% LTV means you can borrow up to $750 per $1,000 collateral. The Liquidation Threshold is higher (e.g., 82.5%) — the point where liquidation actually happens.

cards.heading: the buffer zone
cards.body: The gap between LTV (75%) and Liquidation Threshold (82.5%) is your safety buffer. If you borrow the maximum immediately, you have only a 7.5% cushion before liquidation. Smart borrowers stay well below max LTV.

cards.text: Rule of thumb: borrow at 50-60% of your max LTV. This gives you room to absorb a 30-40% price drop without getting liquidated.

cards.heading: variable rate
cards.body: Changes based on pool utilization — when demand is high, rates spike. Good when you expect rates to stay low or you plan to repay quickly. Most DeFi borrowing uses variable rates.

cards.heading: stable rate
cards.body: Locks in a rate for predictability, but typically starts higher than the current variable rate. Some protocols (like Aave) offer this, though it can be rebalanced in extreme conditions.

cards.text: Supply APY is almost always lower than Borrow APY — the difference is the protocol's spread and reserve factor. This is how lending protocols generate revenue.
